elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by Sparkling..." — the cap is expressed as "each party's", so it binds Garman (Vendor) and Sparkling (Customer) alike; the retained mutual "either party" framing is consistent.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap reads only "the fees paid or payable by Sparkling under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim"; there is no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor anywhere in Section 15.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained: "In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages..." — mutual on its face.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Retained: "The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14." Section 14 is identified as the confidentiality section; because the carve-out is framed against "this Section 15", it lifts the newly inserted cap as well as the indirect-damages exclusion.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No carve-out for data protection or security obligations appears in the rendered Section 15; the only carve-outs are Sections 13/14 and the new gross negligence / wilful misconduct sentence.
Retained carve-out for "breaches of Sections 13 and 14", Section 13 being the IP indemnity; the carve-out is anchored to "this Section 15" and therefore reaches the inserted aggregate cap.
Inserted: "The limitations of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to a party's gross negligence or wilful misconduct."
Inserted: "...shall not apply to a party's gross negligence or wilful misconduct."
The word "fraud" does not appear in the rendered Section 15; the new carve-out sentence stops at gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No express carve-out for a party's infringement of the other party's IP rights; the Section 13 carve-out is an indemnity cross-reference (third-party IP claims), not a party-on-party IP infringement carve-out.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing in the inserted language states that Sparkling's obligation to pay fees is not "damages" subject to the cap; the cap as drafted arguably limits Customer's payment liability, but that is not the required express exclusion.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "Each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — symmetric cap; no retained sentence states Customer's liability is unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable by Sparkling under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 12-month fees basis; "fees" is used generically (uncapitalised, all amounts under the Agreement/Fee Schedule), so the cap is not illusory.
Retained: "The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14" (Section 13 = IP indemnity); the carve-out is section-wide and so lifts the new cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Same section-wide carve-out reaches Section 14 (confidentiality) and, being framed against "this Section 15", excludes those breaches from the inserted aggregate cap.
Inserted second sentence expressly disapplies the Section 15 limitations to "a party's gross negligence".
Inserted second sentence expressly disapplies the Section 15 limitations to "wilful misconduct".

reasons: Fallback is complete: the two inserted sentences supply the missing mutual 12-month fees cap and the gross negligence / wilful misconduct carve-outs, and the retained "this Section 15" carve-out for Sections 13 and 14 automatically lifts the new cap for indemnification and confidentiality.

Preferred is not reached and the finding correctly does not claim it: no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, no data protection/security, fraud or other-party-IP-infringement carve-outs, and no statement that Customer's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.

Minimal: nothing existing was deleted or paraphrased, the favourable mutual indirect-damages exclusion and the Sections 13/14 carve-out are retained, and the insertion adds no survival tail, procedure, damages categories or other extras beyond the two selected fallback gaps.

Intent preserved: the exclusive-remedy sentence, the risk-allocation recital and the Section 13/14 carve-out all continue to operate consistently with a monetary cap; no cross-reference is left dangling and "fees" is used generically rather than as an undefined capitalised term.

Verification caveat for the drafter: the indemnification and confidentiality elements rest entirely on Sections 13 and 14 being the IP indemnity and confidentiality sections — confirm those headings, because if either cross-reference is to a different subject the fallback carve-outs fail and must be stated expressly (e.g. "...shall not apply to a party's indemnification obligations, breach of confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct").

Cosmetic point only (not a deviation): the heading "LIMITATION OF GARMAN'S LIABILITY" now sits above an expressly mutual cap; the body's "each party"/"either party" language controls, but consider retitling to "Limitation of Liability" if the counterparty raises it.

Optional uplift if negotiating room exists: add the USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor and carve out data protection/security, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP, plus a sentence that Customer's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.
